correctness.rationale: For every symmetric absolute normalized N_ψ, its full linear isometry group contains the eight signed coordinate permutations. If H=√q is any candidate Euclidean pullback with N_ψ≤H≤dN_ψ after scalar normalization, then N_ψ²≤q(gx)≤d²N_ψ² for each group element g. Averaging preserves both inequalities and yields a strictly positive scalar quadratic form c(x²+y²), showing no tilted or anisotropic ellipse improves over the coordinate Euclidean circle. The assumed one-sided Euclidean comparison with midpoint-maximal ratio implies the optimal BM distortion M is respectively √2 ψ(1/2) or 1/(√2 ψ(1/2)); the minimum ratio is 1 on axes. Zuo (2012) Theorems 2.2 and 2.3 state the matching Ptolemy value M² under the corresponding hypotheses. Direct source theorem and its normalization were inspected. Thus C_Pt=d_BM², including ψ=ψ₂ and ℓp² checks; no finite sampling is substituted for the finite-group averaging proof.
residual_risks: Only real two-dimensional symmetric absolute normalized norms with one-sided Euclidean comparison and midpoint extremum.

value.rationale: A single structural symmetry-plus-midpoint test evaluates two conceptually different natural invariants on an infinite class of Banach planes. The proof certifies globally optimal Euclidean distortion over all linear maps, so it is a reusable geometric bridge rather than a one-off table recomputation. The required group averaging is elementary but yields a nontrivial cross-invariant identity.

limitations: Symmetry ψ(t)=ψ(1−t) and the midpoint extremum are necessary hypotheses of the given theorem, not asserted for all absolute norms.
